We deploy the api service with a canary that takes 5% of traffic for 20 minutes before full rollout, because the March 2026 outage reached every customer within two minutes of a direct rollout. The production Kubernetes cluster is named tl-prod-euw1 and runs in the europe-west1 region. The staging cluster tl-stage-euw1 is rebuilt from scratch every Sunday at 03:00 UTC, so nothing stateful may live there. Helm upgrades of the api chart fail with 'field is immutable' if the Deployment's selector labels change; the selector must be left as app.kubernetes.io/name=api. Every Helm release name equals the chart name plus the environment, for example api-prod or worker-stage. Rollbacks are done with helm rollback to the previous revision, never by redeploying an older image tag by hand, so the release history stays truthful. The deploy window for production was Tuesday and Thursday 09:00 to 15:00 CET until 2026-05-31. Since 2026-06-01 production deploys are allowed Monday to Thursday 09:00 to 16:00 CET; Friday deploys stay forbidden. The worker pods need terminationGracePeriodSeconds of at least 120, otherwise invoice PDF jobs are killed mid-render during a rollout. The ingress controller is ingress-nginx 1.11 and terminates TLS with certificates issued by cert-manager from Let's Encrypt. Cert-manager renewal failed silently in August 2026 because the ClusterIssuer's ACME account email pointed at a deleted mailbox. Container images are tagged with the full git commit SHA, never with latest, so a running pod can be traced back to its commit. The api Deployment runs 6 replicas in production with a HorizontalPodAutoscaler that scales between 6 and 18 on 65% CPU. kubectl port-forward to the production database is blocked by a NetworkPolicy; use the bastion pod db-bastion in the ops namespace instead. We chose Argo CD over Flux in January 2026 because Argo's UI let the on-call reviewer see drift without cluster credentials. Argo CD syncs the tl-prod-euw1 cluster from the deploy/prod directory of the infra repository every three minutes. Argo CD marks the api application OutOfSync forever if the HPA changes spec.replicas; the Deployment manifest must omit replicas. Node pools in production use e2-standard-8 machines; the pdf-render pool uses c2-standard-16 because rendering is CPU bound. After moving pdf rendering to the c2-standard-16 pool, the p95 invoice render time fell from 4.1 s to 1.7 s. Secrets reach pods through the External Secrets Operator from Google Secret Manager; no secret is ever committed to the infra repository, even encrypted. An ExternalSecret refresh does not restart pods; after rotating a secret, run kubectl rollout restart on the Deployment that mounts it. The blue-green switch for the marketing site is a Cloud DNS record change with a TTL of 60 seconds. Database migrations run as a Kubernetes Job named migrate-<sha> before the api rollout starts, and the rollout waits for the Job to succeed. Pod startup takes 38 seconds on average, of which 30 seconds is the JVM warming the invoice template cache. The primary database is PostgreSQL 16 on Cloud SQL, instance tl-pg-prod, with one synchronous standby in a second zone. Before the upgrade the database ran PostgreSQL 13; the upgrade to 16 happened on 2026-03-14 with 11 minutes of write downtime. After the upgrade to PostgreSQL 16, the nightly ledger aggregation query got 3x faster because of incremental sort. After the PostgreSQL 16 upgrade, run ANALYZE on every table, because pg_upgrade does not carry planner statistics and the first day's plans were terrible. Every table has a created_at and updated_at column of type timestamptz, set by the database, never by the application. We use UUIDv7 primary keys instead of bigserial so ids sort by creation time and can be generated by clients before insert. Adding a column with a volatile default rewrites the whole table; on the invoices table that took a lock for 9 minutes in staging. Indexes on large tables are created with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, and the migration must not run inside a transaction for that statement. The invoices table holds about 410 million rows and is partitioned by month on issued_at. Old monthly partitions of invoices older than 7 years are detached and exported to cold storage, because the retention law requires 7 years. The connection pooler is PgBouncer in transaction mode with a pool of 80 server connections per database. With PgBouncer in transaction mode, session-level SET statements and prepared statements leak between clients; use SET LOCAL inside a transaction. The ledger_entries table had 31% bloat in July 2026 because autovacuum could not keep up with updates to the status column. Ledger entries are append-only: a correction is a new reversing entry, never an UPDATE, so the ledger can be audited. Point-in-time recovery for tl-pg-prod is configured with 14 days of WAL retention. The read replica lags up to 40 seconds under the nightly batch, so reports that must be exact read from the primary.
